rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_supervised-claude-agentic: proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=3, proj_kernel=3, proj_sx=0.01, proj_sy=0.3, proj_sr=0.0005, img_kernel=5, img_sx=0.5, img_sy=0.5, img_sr=0.02, lr=0.005, epochs=12, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=480, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-5 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). BASE = iter-2 BEST (proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=3, 12 params, hr 0.028237) -- NOT iter-4 flat proj_n_bf=2 NOR iter-3 regressed img_n_bf=6. ONE KNOB: train_n 200->480 (DATA-COVERAGE lever -- the only untried axis). epochs traded 24->12 to hold the HARD 20-min wall AND keep grad-steps near parity (480*12=5760 vs iter-2 200*24=4800) so this isolates DATA COVERAGE from extra optimization. MECHANISM VERIFIED (REQUIRED before train_n lever): solver_dual_ddomain_bilateral_supervised.py build_dataset calls load_val_split(split=train, n=train_n) then torch.randperm(train_noisy.shape[0]) per epoch -- a FIXED stratified subset reshuffled each epoch, NOT RotatingSubsetDataset. At train_n=200 the net sees only ~35%% of the 579-slice train pool (same fixed-subset mechanism CONFIRMED-POSITIVE for uswin +0.030 and dual_domain_supervised +0.034). So train_n IS load-bearing here. (The iter-1 rationale claim that the loader rotates the ps-pool was WRONG -- the code is a fixed subset.) SIX-BOX (NUMBERS, hr=metric of record): (1) iter-1 hr 0.027984 SSIM 0.91918 254.3s ep8 12p; iter-2 hr 0.028237 SSIM 0.91916 449.6s ep24 12p = BEST; iter-3 hr 0.0 SSIM 0.90569 574.3s img_n_bf=6 21p = REGRESSED (image-domain capacity DESTABILIZED); iter-4 hr 0.028237 SSIM 0.91916 520.7s proj_n_bf=2 15p = FLAT. (2) LIMITER: every IN-ARCHITECTURE knob exhausted+flat -- epochs inert (8->24), image-domain capacity HURTS (img_n_bf 3->6 -> hr 0), projection-domain capacity flat (proj_n_bf 1->2). The 12-param bilateral is pinned at hr~0.028 by every scalar/capacity move. The ONE untouched axis is DATA COVERAGE (train_n frozen 200 = 35%% of pool). (3) ONE KNOB = train_n 200->480 (epochs 24->12 is the budget-trade to hold the wall, kept near grad-step parity -- not a second hypothesis). (4) HYPOTHESIS: train_n 200->480 (83%% vs 35%% of the 579-slice pool) lifts hr above 0.028237, mirroring the fixed-subset trainers uswin (+0.030) and dual_domain_supervised (+0.034 -> Mayo champion), because more anatomy variety lets the supervised-MSE gradient drive the BF sigmas toward a better RMSE-optimum. This is the SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE remaining experiment -- it definitively answers data-limited vs structural-ceiling for this solver. NUMERIC FALSIFIER: if hr stays <=0.030 (flat) at train_n=480, the 12-param bilateral has TOO LITTLE CAPACITY to exploit more data (exactly like wu_2015 hr 0.0508->0.0411 and hammernik_vn hr 0 which BOTH FAILED this lever) -> FILE THE STRUCTURAL-CEILING VERDICT: dd_bilat_sup is capacity-limited NOT data-limited, hr~0.028 is the few-param-bilateral structural ceiling on real 2304-view Mayo LDCT. (5) BUDGET: HARD 1200s train+score. Measured: iter-1 254.3s ep8/tn200, iter-2 449.6s ep24/tn200 -> 16 extra epochs = 195.3s -> ~12.2s/epoch@tn200, fixed cost (214-slice val + fig setup) ~157s. Per-epoch ~ train_n, so tn480 -> ~29.3s/epoch. ep12@tn480 -> est ~157 + 12*29.3 = ~509s << 1200s (max-epoch ceiling at this train_n ~35; ep12 leaves wide margin). val_n=214 KEPT, grad_clip=1.0 KEPT, all sigmas/kernels/lr/lambda_neg/seed identical to iter-2. 30-min sbatch wall = SLURM net. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (mayo_per_sample_setup/_fbp, per-sample pipe.R_full swap), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; NO fov= override).
